_meta.note: The second history of shtetl, branch v2: foundations and houses (containers and systems alike) as actors over ZFS. A foundation is one dataset whose rolls are snapshots; a house rolls onto each new foundation version into a new dataset named for it, and switches to it when stopped; a failed patch or rebase stalls that one object; zlake converges to zrun; old versions are pruned by count. The plan is implementation-plan.md beside this file, the author's words its section 18; open-questions.md waits on the author. Paths are relative to the shtetl repository root. Drive this file with tools/tracker.py (its default file) or tools/tracker.py --file sprints/sprint-1/shtetl-sprint-1.json <cmd>. STATE 2026-10-18: draft for ruling. The issues of M0 are written; those of M1 to M7 are written at the M0 ruling (rulings-1), since their files depend on the runtime chosen.
_meta.first_history: branch main (4c0f2c7): its docs/planning.md rulings and probe results are evidence; its code is not carried except the configuration language (plan section 12)
_meta.terminology: house = a container or a system; version = one dataset of a house, cloned from one foundation version; live = the version a house runs from; ready = rolled and not yet live; roll = a foundation's next build, or a house's saves replayed onto a newer foundation version into a new version; switch = stop, final save, catch up, switch the link or bootfs, start; stall = an object that stopped rolling and told the person; shake = merge a recipe's layers into the shaken recipe, injected read-only into what it built; beam = zlake converging to zrun; owner = the space where a dataset is written.

milestones.M0: the probes and the spike have run on the box, open-questions.md is answered, and the runtime is chosen
milestones.M1: skeleton: the runtime's tree, its gate and make check; the ZFS boundary with its fake; the daemon, an actor that starts from ZFS after a crash, and the command's socket
milestones.M2: shake: the configuration language carried and trimmed; a shaken recipe made and injected
milestones.M3: foundations: a real roll on the box, a stall and a retry, pkg, the builder
milestones.M4: containers: create, save, pkg, roll, switch, stall and resolve; a real jail rolled across two foundation versions on the box
milestones.M5: beam and prune: convergence, resume after a cut, the counts, a restore as a test
milestones.M6: systems: outer space, boot environments, a switch through a reboot, on a VM

_meta.worklogs: sprints/sprint-1/issue-docs/<key>.md, written when the code lands. See the Worklogs section of CLAUDE.md.

_schema.purpose: Field vocabulary for every issue object in this file. Use these exact terms; do not invent synonyms.

issue_fields.description: required, string. What to build and how to verify it.
issue_fields.requires: required, array of issue keys from THIS file. Empty array means no dependency.
issue_fields.milestone: required, the milestone this issue must be complete for, from _meta.milestones.
issue_fields.expected_changed_files: required, array of paths relative to the repository root.
issue_fields.provides: required, string. What the rest of the sprint can rely on once this is tested.
issue_fields.estimated_size: required, one of: small | medium | large.
issue_fields.note: optional, string. Append with tracker.py note; never replace without cause.

status.code: implementation written and compiling, not yet exercised
status.testing: being exercised; tests being written or findings being fixed

new-history.description: The second history, asked 2026-10-18: branch v2 made with no parent, holding CLAUDE.md (the author's sentence first, then the zfs rebase project's rules carried over), LICENSE (main's, unchanged), a short README.md, tools/tracker.py (the zfs rebase project's scripts/tracker.py with this file as its default) and this sprint folder: implementation-plan.md, open-questions.md, this tracker. Branch main untouched. Verify: tracker.py list and show read this file; every file ASCII.
new-history.provides: A tree, its rules and a tracker that every later issue lands into.

probe-harness.description: The box harness for M0's probes, after main's probes/ (972314c) and tests/box/send.sh (90f58e7), written fresh: sudo sh probes/run.sh [P1 ...] runs the named probes (all by default) on throwaway pools over swap-backed memory disks, refuses to start if a pool of its names exists, and destroys only what it made. Every check prints ok or failed with its probe and cell; the log opens with the shtetl commit it ran at and ends with '== N ok, M failed'. The box commits the log under probes/results/<host>-<time>/ and pushes it (su to SUDO_USER, pull --rebase, push; SEND=no keeps it local). Verify: sh -n on the mac; on the box, run.sh with no probe prints the header and '== 0 ok, 0 failed', and leaves no pool or memory disk behind.
probe-harness.provides: Any probe runs on the box (or the VM) and its log comes back as a commit.

probe-resume.description: P1 (plan section 14): between two md pools standing for zrun and zlake, a full send, an incremental and a clone stream (a house version cloned from a foundation snapshot the lake already has), each received resumable (zfs receive -s, which shtetl will reach as lzc_receive_resumable), each cut part way by killing the sender, each resumed from receive_resume_token (zfs send -t), each ending with the source's guids. Also: a dataset holding a token refuses a fresh receive until it is resumed or aborted (-A), so 'resume if there is a token, else send' is the whole rule. Verify: the probe's cells green on the box.
probe-resume.provides: Evidence for section 8.1: a beam cut anywhere converges on the next attempt with nothing destroyed.

probe-live-link.description: P2: a jail created with path=/containers/H where H is a symlink to v1 (a dataset mounted at /containers/v1, a minimal tree enough to run /bin/sh); the link switched to v2 with rename(2) while the jail runs; the jail stays on v1 (a file written inside lands in v1; jls -n path shows v1's path); jail -r, then jail -c, lands in v2; mount.devfs mounts under the resolved path and jail -r unmounts it; jexec works throughout. Verify: the probe's cells green on the box.
probe-live-link.provides: Evidence for section 7.4 and open question 6: a container's switch is one rename of a link.

probe-house-data.description: P5: a house's own dataset v1/www with three saves; v2/www cloned from v1/www@final; v2/www promoted; v1 destroyed whole; v2/www holds v1/www's saves and its contents; a lake copy of v1/www converged before the promote and of v2/www after it, incrementally where ZFS allows and with whatever it needs where it does not (recorded either way). Verify: the probe's cells green on the box.
probe-house-data.provides: Evidence for sections 7.1 and 8.2: a house's own data moves to a new version by clone and promote, and the lake can follow.

probe-roll-live.description: P6: a house version with three saves of real edits (files added, changed, removed, and one edit that conflicts with the foundation's change and is answered); replayed onto a newer foundation version into a new dataset with zfs_rebase as plan 7.2 step 2 says, while the live version takes a fourth save; the fourth caught up as 7.3 step 3 says; the result compared, tree and attributes, with a replay of all four done at once while nothing ran. Needs zfs_rebase with -m (69d8223 or later) installed on the box. Verify: the probe's cells green on the box.
probe-roll-live.provides: Evidence for sections 7.2 and 7.3: rolling while live and catching up at the switch gives the same tree as rolling while stopped.

probe-boot-envs.description: P3, on a FreeBSD 15.1 VM with root on ZFS that the author provides: two system versions under a systems dataset of the boot pool, each with var and usr/local children, roots mountpoint=/ canmount=noauto; bootfs set to one, rebooted, then the other; each boots with its own children mounted (rc.d/zfsbe) and none of the other's; the loader's boot environment menu lists both and boots either by hand; bectl list shows them. Verify: the probe's cells green on the VM, its reboots driven by the probe across runs.
probe-boot-envs.provides: Evidence for section 7.4: a system's versions are boot environments and its switch is bootfs.

probe-outer-space.description: P4, on the P3 VM: the outer space protocol as ruled 2026-10-15 (a swap-backed memory disk made a pool, the current root sent into it, vfs.root.mountfrom set, reboot -r); an rc script in the sent root that, finding / on the memory pool, snapshots a dataset of the disk pool, sets bootfs to the other version and reboots for real; the machine comes up on the new bootfs. Records how long the send and the reroot take and how large the memory disk had to be. Verify: the probe's cells green on the VM.
probe-outer-space.provides: Evidence for section 7.4: a system stops into outer space, switches there, and comes back on the new version.

spike-port.description: S1 (plan section 14): an Elixir release built on FreeBSD 15.1 from lang/elixir, holding a supervisor and a gen_statem that rolls a toy foundation (write a file, snapshot, clone the snapshot, send it to a second md pool) through a C port: one process speaking the external term format over stdin and stdout with erl_interface's ei, calling libzfs_core (lzc_snapshot, lzc_clone, lzc_send, lzc_receive) and returning nvlist facts as terms, no text. The actor is killed at each step and started again, and finds where it stood from ZFS alone. Measured and written in spike/README.md: the release's size on disk, resident memory idle, start time, the port's round trip. Verify: the spike's cells green on the box. Its code stays in spike/ until the ruling decides its fate.
spike-port.provides: The numbers and the experience section 10's choice is made from.

spike-outer-space.description: S2: the S1 release started by rc on P4's memory-disk root, finding its toy foundation's state on the disk pool and finishing a roll there before the real reboot. Measured: its start time on the memory disk. Verify: the cells green on the VM; the numbers in spike/README.md.
spike-outer-space.provides: Evidence that the chosen runtime can carry a system's switch through outer space.

rulings-1.description: The M0 ruling: the author's answers to open-questions.md and the choice of runtime, quoted in plan section 18 in their words and folded into sections 2 to 17 (each PROPOSAL marker settled one way or the other); the probes' and the spike's results folded in where they confirm or overturn a section; CLAUDE.md given the chosen language's rules if it is not C; the issues of M1 to M7 written into this file with requires, files and verification. Verify: the author reads the folded plan and says go.
rulings-1.provides: A ruled plan, a chosen runtime and the issues of M1 to M7.
